title.zh: 卷五十八 列傳第十八 王惠
title.en: Volume 58 Biographies 18: Wang Hui, Xie Hongwei, Wang Qiu
title.raw: 卷五十八 列傳第十八 王惠 Volume 58 Biographies 18: Wang Hui, Xie Hongwei, Wang Qiu

sentences.zh: 列傳第十八 王惠謝弘微王球

translations.literal: Biographies 18: Wang Hui, Xie Hongwei, Wang Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 18: Wang Hui, Xie Hongwei, and Wang Qiu.

sentences.zh: 王惠，字令明，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, style name Lingming, a man of Langya Linyi, was a paternal cousin once removed of Grand Tutor Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, styled Lingming, came from Langya Linyi and was a distant cousin of Grand Tutor Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 祖劭，車騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Shao had served as General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父默，左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Mo was Left Household Grandee of the Luminous Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Mo was Left Household Grandee of the Luminous Hall.

sentences.zh: 惠幼而夷簡，為叔父司徒謐所知。

translations.literal: From youth Hui was serene and unadorned; he was appreciated by his uncle, Minister over the Masses Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was placid and unpretentious even as a boy, and his uncle Wang Mi, Minister over the Masses, took notice of him.

sentences.zh: 恬靜不交遊，未嘗有雜事。

translations.literal: Quiet and still, he did not associate in social rounds and never had miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He lived quietly and kept no company, and never busied himself with extraneous matters.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝瞻才辯有風氣，嘗與兄弟群從造惠，談論鋒起，文史間發，惠時相酬應，言清理遠，瞻等慚而退。

translations.literal: Xie Zhan of Chen Commandery was talented in debate and possessed bearing; once he visited Hui with his brothers and kinsmen of his clan; thrusts of discussion rose sharp, and historical and literary remarks broke out in turn; Hui responded from time to time; his words were clear and reasoning far-reaching; Zhan and the others retired in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhan of Chen Commandery was eloquent and commanding; once he and his brothers and cousins called on Hui, talk flared, history and literature poured forth, and Hui answered in measured turns with discourse so lucid and penetrating that Zhan and his party withdrew abashed.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞其名，以問其從兄誕，誕曰：「惠後來秀令，鄙宗之美也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu heard his name and inquired of his elder cousin of his clan Dan; Dan said, "Hui is a late-blooming splendid fellow—the glory of our humble clan."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard of him, he asked his elder cousin Wang Dan, who said, "Hui is a late-blooming talent—the finest ornament of our house."

sentences.zh: 即以為行太尉參軍事，府主簿，從事中郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made Acting Retainer to the Grand Commandant, chief clerk of the bureau, and Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was accordingly appointed Acting Retainer to the Grand Commandant, bureau chief clerk, and Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 世子建府，以為征虜長史，仍轉中軍長史。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent established his bureau, he was made Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers Barbarians and shortly thereafter transferred to Chief Clerk of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent opened his staff, Hui became Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, then was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 時會稽內使劉懷敬之郡，送者傾京師，惠亦造別，還過從弟球。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Huaijing, Interior Attendant of Kuaiji, was going to his commandery; those who saw him off filled the capital; Hui also went to bid farewell, and on returning passed by his younger cousin of his clan Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Huaijing, Interior Attendant of Kuaiji, was leaving for his post, the whole capital turned out to see him off; Hui went as well, and on his way back stopped at his cousin Wang Qiu's.

sentences.zh: 球問：「向何所見？」

translations.literal: Qiu asked, "What did you just see?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiu asked, "What did you see on your way back?"

sentences.zh: 惠曰：「惟覺即時逢人耳。」

translations.literal: Hui said, "Only that everywhere I met people at once."
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "Only that I kept running into people at every turn."

sentences.zh: 常臨曲水，風雨暴至，座者皆馳散，惠徐起，姿貌不異常日。

translations.literal: Once at the Winding Water gathering, a violent storm burst upon them; those seated all scattered in flight; Hui rose slowly, his bearing no different from an ordinary day.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a gathering by the Winding Water, a sudden storm struck; everyone at the table bolted, but Hui rose unhurriedly, his composure unchanged from any ordinary day.

sentences.zh: 世子為荊州，惠長史如故。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent took charge of Jingzhou, Hui remained chief clerk as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent went to Jingzhou, Hui continued as chief clerk as before.

sentences.zh: 領南郡太守，不拜。

translations.literal: He was made concurrent Administrator of Nan Commandery but did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the concurrent post of Administrator of Nan Commandery but declined to take office.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建，當置郎中令，高祖難其人，謂傅亮曰：「今用郎中令，不可令減袁曜卿也。」

translations.literal: When the Song state was first established and a Director of Palace Retainers was to be appointed, Gaozu found the choice difficult; he said to Fu Liang, "For Director of Palace Retainers today, one cannot let the post fall below Yuan Yaoqing."
translations.idiomatic: When the Song state was first established and a Director of Palace Retainers had to be chosen, Gaozu found no one satisfactory and told Fu Liang, "Whoever fills this post now must not rank below Yuan Yaoqing."

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「吾得其人矣。」

translations.literal: Then he said, "I have found the man."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "I have my man."

sentences.zh: 乃以惠居之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he installed Hui in the office.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Hui to the post.

sentences.zh: 遷世子詹事，轉尚書，吳興太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, then transferred to be Director of the Masters of Writing and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, then became Director of the Masters of Writing and Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 謝弘微，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Xie Hongwei was a man of Yangxia in Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hongwei was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖韶，車騎司馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was a Major of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xie Shao had been Major of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父思，武昌太守。

translations.literal: His father Si was Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie Si served as Administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 從叔峻，司空琰第二子也，無後，以弘微為嗣。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousin Jun, the second son of Minister of Works Yan, had no heir, and Hongwei was made his successor.
translations.idiomatic: His father's younger cousin Xie Jun, second son of Minister of Works Xie Yan, died without heirs, and Hongwei was adopted as his successor.

sentences.zh: 弘微本名密，犯所繼內諱，故以字行。

translations.literal: Hongwei's original name was Mi; it violated the taboo name of the family he succeeded into, so he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei had originally been named Mi, but that name violated his adoptive family's taboo, so he was known by his style name instead.

sentences.zh: 童幼時，精神端審，時然後言。

translations.literal: In childhood his spirit was composed and careful; he spoke only when the moment was right.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he was grave and composed, and spoke only when the occasion called for it.

sentences.zh: 所繼叔父混名知人，見而異之，謂思曰：「此兒深中夙敏，方成佳器。

translations.literal: His adoptive uncle Hun was famed for knowing men; seeing him he was struck with wonder and said to Si, "This boy is inwardly gifted with early keenness and will become a fine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: His adoptive uncle Xie Hun, renowned for judging character, was astonished at the sight of him and told Si, "This child is gifted beyond his years and will prove a treasure.

sentences.zh: 有子如此，足矣。」

translations.literal: To have a son like this is enough."
translations.idiomatic: A son like this is enough for any man."

sentences.zh: 年十歲出繼。

translations.literal: At age ten he left his birth family to succeed the other line.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of ten he was sent out to succeed the other branch of the family.

sentences.zh: 所繼父於弘微本緦麻，親戚中表，素不相識，率意承接，皆合禮衷。

translations.literal: The adoptive father's relation to Hongwei was originally that of distant kin in the fifth degree; relatives and cousins on both sides had never known one another, yet he received them all as inclination led, and everything accorded with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: His adoptive father's kinship with him had been only the most distant cousinage; relatives and cousins on both sides had never met, yet he received them all as his heart prompted, and every gesture accorded with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，襲峻爵建昌縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yixi era he inherited Jun's title as Marquis of Jianchang County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yixi era he inherited Jun's marquisate of Jianchang County.

sentences.zh: 弘微家素貧儉，而所繼豐泰，唯受書數千卷，國吏數人而已，遺財祿秩，一不關豫。

translations.literal: Hongwei's own family had always been poor and frugal, while the line he succeeded was rich and ample; he accepted only several thousand scrolls of books and a few clerks of the fief—he had no part in the inherited wealth, stipends, or ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei's birth family had always been poor, while the household he succeeded was wealthy; he took only a few thousand books and a handful of fief clerks, and would have nothing to do with the inherited property, stipends, or offices.

sentences.zh: 混聞而驚歎，謂國郎中令漆凱之曰：「建昌國祿，本應與北舍共之，國侯既不措意，今可依常分送。」

translations.literal: Hun heard of this and marveled, saying to the fief's Director of Palace Retainers Qi Kaizhi, "The revenues of the Jianchang fief ought to be shared with the northern household; since the marquis takes no heed of them, you may now distribute them according to custom."
translations.idiomatic: When Hun heard this he was astonished and told the fief's Director of Retainers, Qi Kaizhi, "The Jianchang revenues ought to be shared with his birth family; since the marquis pays them no mind, distribute them as usual from now on."

sentences.zh: 弘微重違混言，乃少有所受。

translations.literal: Hongwei, loath to go against Hun's words, then accepted a small portion.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to defy Hun outright, Hongwei accepted only a modest share.

sentences.zh: 混風格高峻，少所交納，唯與族子靈運、瞻、曜、弘微並以文義賞會。

translations.literal: Hun's manner was lofty and severe; he admitted few associations, associating in literary appreciation only with his clansmen Lingyun, Zhan, Yao, and Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's bearing was lofty and austere; he admitted few companions, and shared literary fellowship only with his kinsmen Lingyun, Zhan, Yao, and Hongwei.

sentences.zh: 嘗共宴處，居在烏衣巷，故謂之烏衣之遊。

translations.literal: They once feasted together in residence in Black Robe Lane, hence it was called the Black Robe gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: They often feasted together in Black Robe Lane, whence their gatherings came to be called the Black Robe company.

sentences.zh: 混五言詩所云「昔為烏衣游，戚戚皆親姪」者也。

translations.literal: This is what Hun's pentasyllabic poem means by "Once we roamed Black Robe Lane—all kin, all nephews close at heart."
translations.idiomatic: This is the company Hun meant in his pentasyllabic lines: "Once we roamed Black Robe Lane—close kin, every one a nephew."

sentences.zh: 其外雖復高流時譽，莫敢造門。

translations.literal: Beyond them, though there were lofty figures of the age in repute, none dared call at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this circle, however eminent the men of the day, none dared knock at his door.

sentences.zh: 瞻等才辭辯富，弘微每以約言服之，混特所敬貴，號曰微子。

translations.literal: Zhan and the others were rich in talent, eloquence, and debate; Hongwei each time won them over with brief words; Hun especially honored and prized him, calling him Master Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and the others were brilliant and argumentative, yet Hongwei regularly won them over with a few well-chosen words; Hun held him in special esteem and called him Master Wei.

sentences.zh: 謂瞻等曰：「汝諸人雖才義豐辯，未必皆愜眾心；

translations.literal: He said to Zhan and the others, "You all, though rich in talent, righteousness, and debate, may not all satisfy the hearts of the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhan and the others, "You may be gifted and eloquent, yet you will not all win every heart;

sentences.zh: 至於領會機賞，言約理要，故當與我共推微子。」

translations.literal: as for grasping the subtle and judging the essential, speaking briefly yet hitting the core of principle—for that you should join me in elevating Master Wei."
translations.idiomatic: but in grasping what matters, judging the essential, and saying little yet striking the heart of things—you should join me in holding up Master Wei."

sentences.zh: 常雲：「阿遠剛躁負氣；

translations.literal: He often said, "A-Yuan is harsh, impetuous, and full of proud spirit;
translations.idiomatic: He often remarked, "A-Yuan is headstrong and quick to take offense;

sentences.zh: 阿客博而無檢；

translations.literal: A-Ke is broad in learning but without restraint;
translations.idiomatic: A-Ke is learned but unrestrained;

sentences.zh: 曜恃才而持操不篤；

translations.literal: Yao relies on talent yet holds his conduct without steadfastness;
translations.idiomatic: Yao trusts in talent but lacks constancy of character;

sentences.zh: 晦自知而納善不周，設復功濟三才，終亦以此為恨；

translations.literal: Hui knows himself yet does not fully embrace what is good; even if his merit were to aid the three capacities of talent, he would still in the end regret this;
translations.idiomatic: Hui is self-aware yet does not fully take in what is good; even if his achievements were to match the worthiest of men, he would still be left with this flaw;

sentences.zh: 至如微子，吾無間然。」

translations.literal: as for Master Wei, I find no fault in him."
translations.idiomatic: but as for Master Wei, I can find no fault in him."

sentences.zh: 又云：「微子異不傷物，同不害正，若年迨六十，必至公輔。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Master Wei in difference does not harm others; in sameness he does not injure what is right; if he lives to sixty, he will surely reach the rank of chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Master Wei stands apart without wounding others, and joins with others without compromising what is right; if he lives to sixty, he will surely reach the highest offices of state."

sentences.zh: 嘗因酣宴之餘，為韻語以獎勸靈運、瞻等曰：「康樂誕通度，實有名家韻，若加繩染功，剖瑩乃瓊瑾。

translations.literal: Once, amid the warmth of a tipsy feast, he composed rhymed lines to encourage and admonish Lingyun, Zhan, and the others, saying, "Kangle is born with comprehensive measure; he truly has the tone of a great house; if the work of binding and dyeing be added, when the lustrous core is split open it will prove jade and gems.
translations.idiomatic: Once, over wine after a feast, he composed rhymed verses to encourage and warn Lingyun, Zhan, and the rest: "Kangle is born with breadth of mind and truly bears a great family's tone; add the finishing discipline, and the polished core within will prove jade.

sentences.zh: 宣明體遠識，穎達且沈儁，若能去方執，穆穆三才順。

translations.literal: Xuanming embodies far-reaching insight; keen and penetrating, yet deep and distinguished; if he can cast off obstinate fixation, the three capacities will follow him in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanming has far-reaching vision, sharp yet deep; shed stubborn fixity, and the three gifts of talent will follow him in harmony.

sentences.zh: 阿多標獨解，弱冠纂華胤，質勝誡無文，其尚又能峻。

translations.literal: A-Duo bears a mark of singular understanding; in his weak-crown years he succeeded a splendid lineage; substance prevails—take warning not to lack ornament; his aspirations can yet be lofty.
translations.idiomatic: A-Duo stands apart in understanding; in early manhood he inherited a splendid line; substance outweighs show—mind that you do not neglect refinement; his aims can still rise high.

sentences.zh: 通遠懷清悟，采采摽蘭訊，直轡鮮不躓，抑用解偏吝。

translations.literal: Tongyuan cherishes clear discernment; flourishing, flourishing he displays orchid fragrance; the straight reins rarely stumble—only restrain them to loosen partial narrowness.
translations.idiomatic: Tongyuan holds to lucid insight, radiant as orchids in bloom; the straight rein seldom falters—only ease it to loosen a narrow heart.

sentences.zh: 微子基微尚，無勌由慕藺，勿輕一簣少，進往將千仞。

translations.literal: Master Wei founds himself on subtle elevation; unwearied, he follows the model of Lin; do not slight a single basket's shortfall—the advance ahead will be a thousand ren.
translations.idiomatic: Master Wei rests on quiet excellence; tireless, he emulates Lin Xiangru; do not despise a single basket's lack—the climb ahead will reach a thousand ren.

sentences.zh: 數子勉之哉，風流由爾振，如不犯所知，此外無所慎。」

translations.literal: You several, strive on! The current of refinement will be revived by you; if you do not transgress what you know, beyond that there is nothing to beware."
translations.idiomatic: Strive on, all of you! The age's refinement will be renewed through you; if you do not violate what you already know, there is nothing else to fear."

sentences.zh: 靈運等並有誡厲之言，唯弘微獨盡褒美。

translations.literal: Lingyun and the others all received words of warning and stern urging; only Hongwei received unmixed praise.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun and the others each received admonition and warning; Hongwei alone was praised without reserve.

sentences.zh: 曜，弘微兄，多，其小字也。

translations.literal: Yao was Hongwei's elder brother; Duo was his childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was Hongwei's elder brother; Duo was his childhood name.

sentences.zh: 遠即瞻字。

translations.literal: Yuan was Zhan's style name.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was Zhan's style name.

sentences.zh: 靈運小名客兒。

translations.literal: Lingyun's childhood name was Guest Boy.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun's childhood name was Ke'er, "Guest Boy."

sentences.zh: 晉世名家身有國封者，起家多拜員外散騎侍郎，弘微亦拜員外散騎，琅邪王大司馬參軍。

translations.literal: In the Jin age, eminent families whose members held state fiefs generally began their careers as Supernumerary Gentlemen of the Palace Cadet, and Hongwei too was made Supernumerary Palace Cadet and Military Assistant to the Grand Marshal of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times, scions of great houses who held state fiefs usually began as Supernumerary Gentlemen of the Palace Cadet; Hongwei received the same appointment and became Military Assistant to the Prince of Langya's Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年，混以劉毅黨見誅，妻晉陵公主改適琅邪王練，公主雖執意不行，而詔其與謝氏離絕，公主以混家事委之弘微。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi, Hun was executed as a partisan of Liu Yi; his wife Princess Jinling was remarried to Wang Lian of Langya; though the princess was resolute in refusing, an edict severed her from the Xie clan, and she entrusted Hun's household affairs to Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yixi, Hun was executed as a partisan of Liu Yi; his wife, Princess Jinling, was ordered to marry Wang Lian of Langya; though she refused, an edict severed her ties to the Xie clan, and she entrusted the household to Hongwei.

sentences.zh: 混仍世宰輔，一門兩封，田業十餘處，僮僕千人，唯有二女，年數歲。

translations.literal: Hun's family had for generations been chief ministers; one household held two enfeoffments; estates in more than ten places; a thousand servants and bondsmen; only two daughters, a few years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Xie family had produced chief ministers for generations; Hun's household held two enfeoffments, estates in more than ten places, and a thousand servants—yet only two daughters, both still small children.

sentences.zh: 弘微經紀生業，事若在公，一錢尺帛出入，皆有文簿。

translations.literal: Hongwei managed the livelihood and enterprises as if they were public affairs; every cash or foot of silk in or out had a written record.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei managed the estates as though they were public office; every coin and every foot of silk that passed in or out was entered in the ledgers.

sentences.zh: 遷通直郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，晉陵公主降為東鄉君，以混得罪前代，東鄉君節義可嘉，聽還謝氏。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate, Princess Jinling was demoted to Lady of Eastern District; because Hun had offended the previous dynasty, yet the Lady of Eastern District's integrity and righteousness were admirable, she was permitted to return to the Xie clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Princess Jinling was demoted to Lady of Eastern District; because Hun had been condemned under the previous regime, yet her constancy was deemed admirable, she was allowed to rejoin the Xie household.

sentences.zh: 自混亡，至是九載，而室宇修整，倉廩充盈，門徒業使，不異平日，田疇墾闢，有加於舊。

translations.literal: From Hun's death to this time was nine years, yet the halls and chambers were in good repair, the granaries full, retainers and laborers no different from ordinary days, and fields opened to cultivation greater than before.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years had passed since Hun's death, yet the house stood in good repair, the granaries were full, servants and tenants went about their work as on any ordinary day, and the fields under cultivation exceeded what there had been before.

sentences.zh: 東鄉君歎曰：「僕射平生重此子，可謂知人。

translations.literal: The Lady of Eastern District sighed and said, "The Vice Director all his life prized this son—he may truly be said to have known men.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Eastern District sighed and said, "The Vice Director valued this boy all his life—he truly knew how to judge men.

sentences.zh: 僕射為不亡矣。」

translations.literal: The Vice Director is not dead."
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director lives on in him."

sentences.zh: 中外姻親，道俗義舊，見東鄉之歸者，入門莫不歎息，或為之涕流，感弘微之義也。

translations.literal: Kinsmen within and without, friends lay and clerical, seeing the Lady of Eastern District's return—all who entered the gate sighed without exception, and some wept for it, moved by Hongwei's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives near and far, lay friends and clerical acquaintances alike—whoever witnessed the Lady of Eastern District's return sighed at the threshold, and some wept, moved by Hongwei's devotion.

sentences.zh: 性嚴正，舉止必循禮度，事繼親之黨，恭謹過常。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and upright; his bearing always followed ritual measure; in serving the kin of the family he had succeeded into, his respect and care exceeded the norm.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and upright by nature, conducted himself always within ritual bounds, and in serving his adoptive kin showed a respect exceeding the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 伯叔二母，歸宗兩姑，晨夕瞻奉，盡其誠敬。

translations.literal: His paternal uncles' two wives, his aunts returned to the clan—morning and evening he attended them with full sincerity and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles' wives, his aunts who had returned to the clan—morning and evening he attended them with complete sincerity.

sentences.zh: 內或傳語通訊，輒正其衣冠。

translations.literal: If within the inner quarters someone passed a message or communication, he would straighten his cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a message was relayed from the inner quarters, he would straighten his cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 婢僕之前，不妄言笑，由是尊卑小大，敬之若神。

translations.literal: Before maidservants and bondsmen he did not speak or laugh at random; thereby great and small, high and low, revered him as a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Before servants he never spoke or laughed lightly; high and low alike revered him as though he were divine.

sentences.zh: 兄曜歷御史中丞，彭城王義康驃騎長史，元嘉四年卒。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yao served as Imperial Censor and Chief Clerk to the Rapid Cavalry General of Prince Yikang of Pengcheng; he died in the fourth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yao had served as Imperial Censor and Chief Clerk to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng's Rapid Cavalry staff; he died in the fourth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 弘微蔬食積時，哀戚過禮，服雖除，猶不啖魚肉。

translations.literal: Hongwei ate vegetables for a long stretch; his grief exceeded ritual propriety; though mourning garments were removed, he still did not eat fish or meat.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei ate only vegetables for a long while, his grief exceeding what ritual required; even after the mourning period ended, he still would not touch fish or meat.

sentences.zh: 沙門釋慧琳詣弘微，弘微與之共食，猶獨蔬素。

translations.literal: The monk Shi Huilin called on Hongwei; Hongwei ate with him yet still took vegetables alone.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huilin called on him; Hongwei dined with him but still ate only plain fare.

sentences.zh: 慧琳曰：「檀越素既多疾，頃者肌色微損，即吉之後，猶未復膳。

translations.literal: Huilin said, "The lay patron has long been frail in health; recently his complexion has declined somewhat; after the auspicious day of mourning's end, he has still not resumed proper meals.
translations.idiomatic: Huilin said, "You have long been frail, and lately your complexion has faded; even after the mourning rites ended, you have not returned to proper meals.

sentences.zh: 若以無益傷生，豈所望於得理。」

translations.literal: If through what brings no benefit one harms life, is that what is hoped for in attaining principle?"
translations.idiomatic: If you harm your health for no good purpose, is that what reason demands?"

sentences.zh: 弘微答曰：「衣冠之變，禮不可逾。

translations.literal: Hongwei replied, "The change of cap and robes—ritual cannot be overstepped.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei answered, "I have changed my cap and robes, and ritual cannot be overstepped.

sentences.zh: 在心之哀，實未能已。」

translations.literal: the grief in the heart truly cannot yet cease."
translations.idiomatic: the grief in my heart truly cannot cease."

sentences.zh: 遂廢食感咽，歔欷不自勝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped eating, choked with feeling, and sobbed beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: He then set aside his food, choked with emotion, and sobbed uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 弘微少孤，事兄如父，兄弟友穆之至，舉世莫及也。

translations.literal: Hongwei was orphaned young; he served his elder brother as a father; the brothers' mutual friendship and harmony reached the utmost—the age had none to equal it.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Hongwei had served his elder brother as a father; the bond between the brothers was the most devoted of their age.

sentences.zh: 弘微口不言人短長，而曜好臧否人物，曜每言論，弘微常以它語亂之。

translations.literal: Hongwei by mouth did not speak of others' faults or merits, while Yao liked to judge people good or bad; whenever Yao discoursed, Hongwei would often confuse the thread with other words.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei never spoke of others' faults or merits, but Yao loved to pass judgment on people; whenever Yao began to criticize someone, Hongwei would divert the conversation.

sentences.zh: 六年，東宮始建，領中庶子，又尋加侍中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Eastern Palace was first established; he headed the Palace Companions and shortly thereafter was additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Eastern Palace was established; he was made head of the Palace Companions and soon after was also appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 弘微志在素官，畏忌權寵，固讓不拜，乃聽解中庶子。

translations.literal: Hongwei's aim lay in plain office; he feared and shunned power and favor; he firmly declined and did not accept investiture, and was therefore permitted to resign as Palace Companion.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei sought only a modest post and shrank from power and favor; he firmly refused the appointment and was allowed to resign as Palace Companion.

sentences.zh: 每有獻替及論時事，必手書焚草，人莫之知。

translations.literal: Whenever he offered remonstrance or discussed affairs of the time, he always wrote by hand and burned the draft—no one knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he offered counsel or discussed affairs of state, he wrote by hand and burned the draft, so that no one ever knew what he had said.

sentences.zh: 上以弘微能營膳羞，嘗就求食。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Hongwei could prepare fine dishes, once came to request a meal.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Hongwei's skill at preparing fine meals, the emperor once came to ask for food.

sentences.zh: 弘微與親故經營，既進之後，親人問上所御，弘微不答，別以餘語酬之，時人比漢世孔光。

translations.literal: Hongwei arranged it with kin and old friends; after it had been presented, kin asked what the emperor had eaten; Hongwei did not answer but responded with other words; men of the time compared him to Kong Guang of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei prepared it with relatives and friends; afterward, when kin asked what the emperor had eaten, Hongwei would not say, but answered with something else; contemporaries compared him to Kong Guang of Han times.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，有疾，解右衛，領太子右衛率，還家。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year he fell ill, resigned the Right Guard, headed the Heir Apparent's Right Guard Command, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year he fell ill, resigned as Right Guard, took the concurrent post of Commander of the Heir Apparent's Right Guard, and went home.

sentences.zh: 議欲解弘微侍中，以率加吏部尚書，固陳疾篤，得免。

translations.literal: It was proposed to relieve Hongwei of Palace Attendant and add Director of the Masters of Writing to his commandership; he firmly declared his illness grave and was excused.
translations.idiomatic: The court proposed to remove him as Palace Attendant and add Director of the Masters of Writing to his commandership; he pleaded grave illness and was excused.

sentences.zh: 九年，東鄉君薨，資財鉅萬，園宅十餘所，又會稽、吳興、琅邪諸處，太傅、司空琰時事業，奴僮猶有數百人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Lady of Eastern District died; assets in the tens of thousands; more than ten garden residences; moreover in Kuaiji, Wuxing, Langya, and other places the estates of Grand Tutor and Minister of Works Yan in their day; bondsmen and servants still numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Lady of Eastern District died, leaving assets in the tens of thousands, more than ten estates, and properties in Kuaiji, Wuxing, Langya, and elsewhere from Grand Tutor Xie Yan's day—hundreds of servants still remained.

sentences.zh: 公私咸謂室內資財，宜歸二女，田宅僮僕，應屬弘微。

translations.literal: Public and private opinion alike held that indoor assets and wealth should go to the two daughters, while fields, residences, and servants ought to belong to Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private opinion alike held that the household goods should go to the two daughters, while the lands, houses, and servants ought to belong to Hongwei.

sentences.zh: 弘微一無所取，自以私祿營葬。

translations.literal: Hongwei took nothing at all and paid for the funeral from his private stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei took nothing and paid for the funeral from his private salary.

sentences.zh: 混女夫殷睿素好樗蒱，聞弘微不取財物，乃濫奪其妻妹及伯母兩姑之分以還戲責，內人皆化弘微之讓，一無所爭。

translations.literal: Hun's son-in-law Yin Rui had always loved gambling; hearing that Hongwei took no property, he usurped his wife's younger sister's and his paternal aunts' shares to pay gaming debts; the women within all followed Hongwei's yielding and contested nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's son-in-law Yin Rui was addicted to gambling; learning that Hongwei took nothing, he seized his wife's sister's and his aunts' shares to pay gaming debts; the women of the household, following Hongwei's example of forbearance, contested nothing.

sentences.zh: 弘微舅子領軍將軍劉湛性不堪其非，謂弘微曰：「天下事宜有裁衷。

translations.literal: Hongwei's nephew by marriage, General of the Forward Armies Liu Zhan, by nature could not bear such wrong; he said to Hongwei, "Affairs under Heaven ought to have balanced judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei's nephew by marriage, Liu Zhan, General of the Forward Armies, could not abide such conduct and told Hongwei, "Affairs under Heaven ought to be judged with balance.

sentences.zh: 卿此不治，何以治官。」

translations.literal: If you do not set this right, how will you govern office?"
translations.idiomatic: If you will not set this right in your own house, how can you govern in office?"

sentences.zh: 弘微笑而不答。

translations.literal: Hongwei smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 或有譏之曰：「謝氏累世財產，充殷君一朝戲責，理之不允，莫此為大。

translations.literal: Someone mocked him, saying, "The Xie clan's wealth accumulated over generations was spent to settle Lord Yin's gaming debts in a single morning—nothing is more unjust in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Someone mocked him, saying, "Generations of Xie wealth were squandered in a morning to pay Yin's gambling debts—nothing could be more unjust.

sentences.zh: 卿親而不言，譬棄物江海以為廉耳。

translations.literal: You are kin yet do not speak—like casting goods into rivers and seas and calling it integrity.
translations.idiomatic: You are kin yet say nothing—as though throwing treasure into the sea and calling it integrity.

sentences.zh: 設使立清名，而令家內不足，亦吾所不取也。」

translations.literal: Even if one establishes a pure name yet leaves the household within wanting—that too is what I would not take."
translations.idiomatic: Even if you win a reputation for purity while leaving your household in want—that is nothing I would admire."

sentences.zh: 弘微曰：「親戚爭財，為鄙之甚。

translations.literal: Hongwei said, "For kin to contend over wealth is the height of baseness.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei said, "For kin to fight over money is the depth of vulgarity.

sentences.zh: 今內人尚能無言，豈可導之使爭。

translations.literal: Now the women within can still hold their tongues—how could one guide them to contention?
translations.idiomatic: The women of the household have held their peace—how could I lead them into quarreling?

sentences.zh: 今分多共少，不至有乏，身死之後，豈復見關。」

translations.literal: Now the shares are many sharing little—there will not be want; after one's body dies, how could it still matter?"
translations.idiomatic: As things stand, many share a little and none will go wanting; after death, what would it matter anyway?"

sentences.zh: 東鄉君葬，混墓開，弘微牽疾臨赴，病遂甚。

translations.literal: At the Lady of Eastern District's burial Hun's tomb was opened; Hongwei, dragging his illness, went in haste to attend, and his illness then grew grave.
translations.idiomatic: At the Lady of Eastern District's funeral Hun's tomb was opened; Hongwei dragged himself there despite his illness, and his condition grew critical.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died, at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 時有一長鬼寄司馬文宣家，云受遣殺弘微，弘微疾增劇，輒豫告文宣。

translations.literal: At the time a tall ghost lodged in Sima Wenxuan's house, saying it had been dispatched to kill Hongwei; as Hongwei's illness worsened, it would forewarn Wenxuan in advance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a tall ghost haunted Sima Wenxuan's house, claiming it had been sent to kill Hongwei; as Hongwei's illness worsened, it would warn Wenxuan in advance.

sentences.zh: 弘微既死，與文宣分別而去。

translations.literal: Once Hongwei had died, it took leave of Wenxuan and departed.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongwei died, it bade Wenxuan farewell and departed.

sentences.zh: 弘微臨終，語左右曰：「有二封書，須劉領軍至，可於前燒之，慎勿開也。」

translations.literal: At the end Hongwei told those beside him, "There are two sealed letters; when the Forward Armies General Liu arrives, burn them before him—take care not to open them."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Hongwei told those beside him, "There are two sealed letters; when General Liu arrives, burn them in his presence—do not open them."

sentences.zh: 書皆是太祖手敕。

translations.literal: The letters were all personal writs of the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The letters were all in the Grand Ancestor's own hand.

sentences.zh: 上甚痛惜之，使二衛千人營畢葬事。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply for him and sent a thousand men from the two guards to complete the funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply and sent a thousand men from the two palace guards to complete the funeral.

sentences.zh: 追贈太常。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand Master of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 子莊，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Zhuang has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuang is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 王球，字倩玉，琅邪臨沂人，太常惠從父弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Qiu, style name Qianyu, a man of Langya Linyi, was a paternal cousin once removed of Grand Tutor Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu, styled Qianyu, came from Langya Linyi and was a distant cousin of Grand Tutor Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 父謐，司徒。

translations.literal: His father Mi was Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Mi was Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 球少與惠齊名，美容止。

translations.literal: Qiu in youth was as famed as Hui for his fine appearance and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Qiu was as renowned as Hui for his handsome bearing.

sentences.zh: 除著作佐郎，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing but declined to take office.

sentences.zh: 尋除琅邪王大司馬行參軍，轉主簿，豫章公世子中軍功曹。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made Acting Military Assistant to the Grand Marshal of the Prince of Langya, then chief clerk, then Merit Officer of the Central Army on the Heir Apparent of the Duke of Yuzhang's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became Acting Military Assistant to the Prince of Langya's Grand Marshal, then chief clerk, then Merit Officer on the Central Army staff of the Duke of Yuzhang's heir.

sentences.zh: 宋國建，初拜世子中舍人。

translations.literal: When the Song state was established he was first appointed Gentleman of the Palace Suite to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song state was founded he was first appointed Gentleman of the Palace Suite to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，仍為太子中舍人，宜都王友，轉諮議參軍，以疾去職。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate he remained Gentleman of the Palace Suite to the Heir Apparent, Friend to the Prince of Yidu, transferred to Advising Military Assistant, and left office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he remained Gentleman of the Palace Suite to the crown prince, became Friend to the Prince of Yidu, then Advising Military Assistant, and resigned on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年，起為義興太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia he was raised to Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia he was recalled to serve as Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 從兄弘為揚州，服親不得相臨，加宣威將軍，在郡有寬惠之美，徙太子右衛率。

translations.literal: His elder cousin of his clan Hong was in Yangzhou; as mourning kin they could not oversee one another; he was given the additional title General Who Proclaims Might; in the commandery he had the reputation of leniency and kindness; he was transferred to Commander of the Heir Apparent's Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Wang Hong was in Yangzhou; as kin in mourning they could not govern one another's territory; Qiu was given the additional title General Who Proclaims Might; in the commandery he won praise for leniency and kindness, then was transferred to Commander of the Heir Apparent's Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中，領冠軍將軍，又領本州大中正，徙中書令，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant, headed the Champion General, also headed the Senior Arbiter of his home province, was moved to Inspector of the Masters of Writing while remaining Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Palace Attendant and Champion General, also served as Senior Arbiter of his home province, then became Inspector of the Masters of Writing while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 球公子簡貴，素不交遊，筵席虛靜，門無異客。

translations.literal: Master Qiu's manner was simple and noble; he never associated in social rounds; his banquet seats were empty and still; no unusual guests at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was simple and self-contained by nature, kept no company, held quiet gatherings with empty seats, and admitted no casual visitors.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射殷景仁、領軍劉湛並執重權，傾動內外，球雖通家姻戚，未嘗往來。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yin Jingren and Forward Armies General Liu Zhan both wielded heavy power and swayed court and countryside; though Qiu was connected by marriage, he never visited them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yin Jingren and Forward Armies General Liu Zhan both wielded great power and swayed the court; though Qiu was connected to them by marriage, he never called on them.

sentences.zh: 頗好文義，唯與琅邪顏延之相善。

translations.literal: He rather loved literary arts; only with Yan Yanzhi of Langya was he on friendly terms.
translations.idiomatic: He cared deeply for literature and had only Yan Yanzhi of Langya as a close friend.

sentences.zh: 居選職，接客甚希，不視求官書疏，而銓衡有序，朝野稱之。

translations.literal: In his selection post he received guests very rarely, did not look at petition letters seeking office, yet his weighing and balance were orderly—court and countryside praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In his appointment post he received few visitors and ignored letters seeking office, yet his selections were fair and orderly, and court and countryside alike praised him.

sentences.zh: 本多羸疾，屢自陳解。

translations.literal: He had always been frail in health and repeatedly petitioned to resign.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been frail and repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，領廬陵王師。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Household Grandee of the Luminous Hall, given the golden seal and purple ribbon, and headed as Preceptor to the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Household Grandee of the Luminous Hall with the golden seal and purple ribbon, and appointed Preceptor to the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 兄子履進利為行，深結劉湛，委誠大將軍彭城王義康，與劉斌、孔胤秀等並有異志，球每訓厲，不納。

translations.literal: His nephew Lü practiced advancing profit as his course, bound himself deeply to Liu Zhan, gave his loyalty to the Great General Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, and with Liu Bin, Kong Yinxiu, and others harbored contrary designs; Qiu admonished him each time but he would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Lü was greedy and ambitious; he attached himself to Liu Zhan, pledged loyalty to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, and with Liu Bin, Kong Yinxiu, and others harbored treasonous designs; Qiu admonished him repeatedly, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 自大將軍從事中郎，轉太子中庶子，流涕訴義康不願違離，以此復為從事中郎。

translations.literal: From Military Assistant to the Great General he was transferred to Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent; weeping, he pleaded to Yikang that he did not wish to be separated, and for this was restored as Military Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from Military Assistant on the Great General's staff to Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent, he wept and begged Yikang not to be parted from him, and was therefore restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚銜之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor harbored strong resentment toward him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor harbored a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 及湛誅之夕，履徒跣告球。

translations.literal: On the night Liu Zhan was executed, Lü came barefoot to inform Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: On the night Liu Zhan was executed, Lü came barefoot to warn Qiu.

sentences.zh: 球命為取履，先溫酒與之，謂曰：「常日語汝，何如？」

translations.literal: Qiu ordered shoes fetched for him, first warmed wine and gave it to him, and said, "What of all I told you on ordinary days?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had shoes brought for him, warmed wine, and said, "What of everything I told you before?"

sentences.zh: 履怖懼不得答，球徐曰：「阿父在，汝亦何憂。」

translations.literal: Lü was afraid and could not answer; Qiu said slowly, "Your uncle is here—what have you to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Lü could not answer; Qiu said calmly, "Your uncle is here—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 命左右：「扶郎還齋。」

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants, "Help the young master back to his quarters."
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants, "Help the young master back to his room."

sentences.zh: 上以球故，履得免死，廢於家。

translations.literal: Because of Qiu, the emperor spared Lü's life and he was disgraced at home.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Qiu, the emperor spared Lü's life and he was disgraced at home.

sentences.zh: 十七年，球復為太子詹事，大夫、王師如故。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Qiu again became Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, while Grandee and Preceptor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Qiu was again appointed Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, retaining his posts as Grandee and Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 未拜，會殷景仁卒，因除尚書僕射，王師如故。

translations.literal: Before he could take office, Yin Jingren died, and he was therefore made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Preceptor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the appointment, Yin Jingren died, and he was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing instead, while remaining Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 素有腳疾。

translations.literal: He had long suffered from a foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suffered from a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書江夏王義恭謂尚書何尚之曰：「當今乏才，群下宜加戮力，而王球放恣如此，恐宜以法糾之。」

translations.literal: Overseer of the Masters of Writing Prince Yigong of Jiangxia said to Director He Shangzhi, "The age lacks talent; those below ought to redouble effort, yet Wang Qiu indulges himself like this—perhaps he should be checked by law."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, Overseer of the Masters of Writing, told Director He Shangzhi, "The court lacks talent and everyone should exert himself, yet Wang Qiu indulges himself like this—perhaps he ought to be called to account by law."

sentences.zh: 尚之曰：「球有素尚，加又多疾，應以淡退求之，未可以文案責也。」

translations.literal: He Shangzhi said, "Qiu has long held pure aims, and moreover many illnesses—one should seek mild withdrawal from him; he cannot yet be faulted on paperwork."
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi replied, "Qiu has always been a man of pure aims, and besides he is often ill; one should expect quiet withdrawal from him, not fault him on paperwork."

sentences.zh: 猶坐白衣領職。

translations.literal: He still sat in plain dress while holding office.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to attend in plain dress while holding office.

sentences.zh: 時群臣詔見，多不即前，卑疏者或至數十日，大臣亦有十餘日不被見者。

translations.literal: At that time when ministers were summoned to audience, many did not advance at once; the low in standing sometimes waited dozens of days; great ministers too sometimes were not received for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: At that time when ministers were summoned to audience, many would not advance promptly; men of low rank sometimes waited dozens of days, and even senior ministers might go more than ten days without being received.

sentences.zh: 唯球輒去，未嘗肯停。

translations.literal: Qiu alone would depart at once and never consent to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu alone would leave at once and never consent to wait.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he died, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 追贈特進、金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Special Advancement, Household Grandee of the Luminous Hall with the golden seal and purple ribbon, and additionally Gentlemen of the Palace Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Special Advancement, Household Grandee of the Luminous Hall with the golden seal and purple ribbon, and additionally Palace Cadet.

sentences.zh: 無子，從孫奐為後。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his grand-nephew Huan was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; his grand-nephew Huan was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 大明末，吳興太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daming era he was Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daming era Huan served as Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 或人問史臣曰：「王惠何如？」

translations.literal: Someone asked the historiographer, "What of Wang Hui?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked the historiographer, "What of Wang Hui?"

sentences.zh: 答之曰：「令明簡。」

translations.literal: The answer was, "Lingming—simple."
translations.idiomatic: The reply was, "Lingming—simple."

sentences.zh: 又問：「王球何如？」

translations.literal: Again asked, "What of Wang Qiu?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "What of Wang Qiu?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「倩玉淡。」

translations.literal: The reply was, "Qianyu—detached."
translations.idiomatic: The reply was, "Qianyu—detached."

sentences.zh: 又問：「謝弘微何如？」

translations.literal: Again asked, "What of Xie Hongwei?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "What of Xie Hongwei?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「簡而不失，淡而不流，古之所謂名臣，弘微當之矣。」

translations.literal: The reply was, "Simple yet without loss, detached yet without dissipation—what the ancients called a famed minister; Hongwei fits that."
translations.idiomatic: The reply was, "Simple yet without loss, detached yet without dissipation—what the ancients called a famed minister; Hongwei is that man."
